items.title: Derek Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995
items.q: We had a nice interview with him a couple of months ago with Bill Hughes.

ctx.x: but then of course nothing stays the same forever, and the studio work disappears now, because, well many different reasons. (a) we all got older; (b) technology put us out of work because they can do things with synthesizers where they don’t need so many live musicians anymore. And so then I read that Frank Foster is back on the road now leading the band.
Yeah. We had a nice interview with him a couple of months ago with Bill Hughes. Tell us about working with Benny Goodman.

Well, what do you want to know? It’s hard to say. I mean without a doubt, Benny was the finest jazz clarinetist — this is all subjective opinion, certainly my opinion — I’ve never heard of anybody that played as well as he did that thrilled me as well. But, given all that, which is a big given, he was a very difficult guy to get along with. None of us really knew why. Either he heard — they say that symphony conductors hear what they want to hear of a piece a fraction of a second before the orchestra plays it,…
